roster_note: The flagship repeatable-storey asset (§6.1). One authored building must yield 5-, 7-, and 9-storey variants via `minfloors`/`maxfloors`.
residential_program: identical apartment or office floors repeated the full height of the slab
one stair core per four bays of slab length, minimum two, expressed as projecting towers with a continuous glazing slot
a landing serving two to four doors at every core on every floor
ground-floor entrance vestibules with an unheated lobby between two door leaves
ground-floor mail, pram and refuse stores off the entrance lobby
a basement pipe gallery running the long axis to the exterior heating main stub
a basement electrical room and a lockable tenant store bay
a roof bulkhead over each stair core with the roof plant clustered against it
circulation: vertical circulation uses encased stair cores at no more than four-bay intervals, landing-connected at both ends
no floor may be reachable only through another dwelling
the basement gallery connects both cores
damage_constraints: the heating main is severed at one visible saddle on the lot
frost damage, burst risers and boarded openings appear only on the bays downstream of the break
both stair cores and the basement route survive
at least one entrance vestibule remains intact and passable
derive all damage and occupation only from the immutable clean master
use an authored fracture with a gravity-consistent rubble apron, never a cleared box and never per-block random deletion

required_manual_checks: the panel joint grid is continuous and unbroken across every elevation
storey bands above the plinth are silhouette-identical
the plinth reads as one block proud on all four elevations
the break in the heating main is findable without entering the building

footprint_drift_exception.reason: The 61x53 source lot is near-square, but the Karsic residential-slab rule requires length >= 3x inhabited height and a viable double-loaded plan. The regional designer preserves the five-storey height, expands length to the next four-block panel bay that meets the ratio, and reduces depth to seven bays (12-block rooms + 3-block corridor + 12-block rooms).
